title: Perfect tensor tests detect relative perfection on algebraic spaces
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces with their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ for the full subcategory with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Derived tensor is computed by K-flat resolutions and derived direct image by K-injective resolutions. A perfect complex is etale locally represented by a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free modules [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ a separated flat finitely presented algebraic space. Here separated means the diagonal is a closed immersion; flatness and local finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts; finite presentation includes quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. Let $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$. Suppose $R\Gamma(X,E\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}^{\mathbf L}K)$ is perfect in $D(A)$ for every perfect $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$, where perfect over $A$ means isomorphic to a bounded complex of finitely generated projective $A$-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Then $K$ is $\operatorname{Spec}A$-perfect: it is pseudo-coherent (etale locally represented by a bounded-above complex of finite free modules) and locally has finite Tor amplitude over $f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}$. The latter means that locally there is a finite interval $[a,b]$ outside which the cohomology of the derived tensor with every module over this inverse-image ring sheaf in degree zero vanishes. In particular $K$ is locally cohomologically bounded below. Global sections are [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology].

source.place: Tag 0GFL, lemma-characterize-relatively-perfect; local lower boundedness from lemma-bounded-on-fibres, preceding it.

proof.text: Each perfect test has a bounded finite-projective $A$-model. Apply [lem-pc-finite-projective-complex-free-model] to obtain a bounded-above finite-free model, so the test is pseudo-coherent by [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-perfect-tests-pseudocoherence]: $f$ is separated flat finitely presented by hypothesis, so $K$ is pseudo-coherent on $X$.

source.place: Tag 0GFL, first two sentences; Tags 0GFJ and 0DII.

proof.text: $X$ is quasi-compact quasi-separated by finite presentation over the affine base. Choose a perfect generator $G$ by [lem-sfb-space-perfect-weak-generator]. Its dual $G^\vee$ is perfect by [lem-sfb-ringed-site-perfect-duality]. The hypothesis at $E=G^\vee$ makes $R\Gamma(X,G^\vee\otimes^{\mathbf L}K)$ perfect, hence bounded below by its bounded projective model. Condition (iii) of [lem-sfb-space-generator-detects-lower-bound] therefore gives $K\in D^+_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$, in particular locally bounded below.

source.place: Tag 0GFL, application of Tag 0GFI; the printed D-minus is corrected to D-plus.

proof.text: Fix a prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$, put $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $Y=X\times_A\operatorname{Spec}k$, and let $i:Y\to X$ be the projection. It is affine as the base change of a morphism between affine schemes; $Y$ is quasi-compact quasi-separated. By [lem-sfb-space-derived-qcoh-pullback-tensor], $Li^*K$ and $Li^*G$ have quasi-coherent cohomology. Also $Li^*G$ is perfect: for an etale $V\to X$ put $Y_V=Y\times_XV$; by [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus], $(Li^*G)|_{Y_V}\cong Li_V^*(G|_V)$. Where $G|_V$ has a bounded model of direct summands of finite free modules, [lem-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-ringed-pullback-model] identifies $Li_V^*$ of it with the termwise pullback, again such a bounded model. The $Y_V$ cover $Y$.

source.place: Tag 0GFL, fibre and perfect pullback; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08H3 (lemma-strictly-perfect-pullback), applied etale locally as in Tag 08H6.

proof.text: For any $F\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$, derived adjunction from [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus] identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(Li^*G[n],F)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(G[n],Ri_*F)$. If these vanish for every $n$, the defining zero-detection property of $G$ gives $Ri_*F=0$. By [lem-sfb-space-affine-derived-pushforward-conservative], $Ri_*$ lands in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$ and reflects the isomorphism of $0\to F$; hence $F=0$. Thus $Li^*G$ is a perfect generator on $Y$.

source.place: Tag 0GFL, use of spaces-perfect.tex Tag 0E4R, remark-pullback-generator (affine case).

proof.text:
By [lem-sfb-space-affine-perfect-hom-base-change], applied to the flat $f$ and $A\to k$, there is an isomorphism in $D(k)$
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Li^*G,Li^*K)\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_X(G,K)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}k.$$
By [lem-sfb-ringed-site-perfect-duality] the latter Hom over $X$ is $R\Gamma(X,G^\vee\otimes^{\mathbf L}K)$, perfect by hypothesis. Its tensor with $k$ is perfect by [lem-sc-perfect-pullback-perfect-residue], and hence has no sufficiently negative cohomology. The Hom base-change node identifies degree-$j$ cohomology with $\operatorname{Hom}(Li^*G,Li^*K[j])$. Condition (ii) of [lem-sfb-space-generator-detects-lower-bound] now shows that $Li^*K$ is bounded below. No common bound over the primes is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0GFL, displayed derived Hom calculation and its boundedness consequence; spaces-perfect.tex Tag 0E4S provides the existing derived Hom base-change form.

proof.text: Every point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is a prime $\mathfrak p$, so steps 2 and 5 provide both lower-boundedness hypotheses of [lem-sfb-space-relative-perfect-fibre-criterion]. Step 1 supplies its pseudo-coherence hypothesis, and $f$ is flat locally finitely presented. The criterion gives finite Tor amplitude locally over $f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}$. Together with pseudo-coherence this is precisely the asserted $\operatorname{Spec}A$-perfection; local lower boundedness was already proved in step 2.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0GFL, lemma-characterize-relatively-perfect, proof; affine conservativity spells out Tag 0E4R, and Tag 0E4S supplies the displayed derived Hom base-change isomorphism.
